[seg_0001] Advisor (0.00-12.08): Good morning, Adrian. Rachel Tan speaking. Thanks for calling. Are you somewhere you can speak privately, and is the line clear enough? We can keep the conversation brief.
[seg_0002] Client (12.48-25.30): Morning, Rachel. Yes, I'm in my office with the door closed. The line is clear. My NRIC is S four five four three four seven two K. My date of birth is 30 April 1997.
[seg_0003] Advisor (25.70-33.58): Thank you. Before we get into the call, is telephone still your preferred way for us to contact you, rather than arranging a meeting?
[seg_0004] Client (33.98-45.07): Telephone is easier, actually. I can step away between consultancy meetings without having to travel to the branch. The product I want to transact in is Summit Global Equity ETF. I want to buy.
[seg_0005] Advisor (45.47-51.77): Noted on the contact arrangement. I recommend buying Summit Global Equity ETF.
[seg_0006] Client (52.16-63.67): Okay, noted. I'm travelling next week, so calls may be a little harder to arrange. I'm around this week, though. If you need another conversation, an afternoon slot would generally be easier.
[seg_0007] Advisor (64.07-73.70): We can arrange future conversations around your availability. When you're away, would you prefer that we leave a callback message, or wait for you to get in touch?
[seg_0008] Client (74.10-82.81): A short callback message is fine. Please don't leave a long message while I'm travelling. I may be in meetings, and I would rather speak directly when I've got somewhere quiet.
[seg_0009] Advisor (83.21-97.57): I'll note that preference for future contact. Let me turn to the prepared points for today's conversation. Let me confirm your objective: you want to build wealth over the long term through diversified exposure to global equities.
[seg_0010] Client (97.97-104.23): I've set aside time for the questions today. No need to rush through them; I just prefer keeping the conversation direct.
[seg_0011] Advisor (104.64-127.43): For Summit Global Equity ETF, a decline in global equity markets can reduce the value of its underlying holdings. During volatile or illiquid markets, its traded price can also differ from its underlying asset value. Do you understand that market declines can reduce the fund's value, and that its traded price may differ from its underlying asset value?
[seg_0012] Client (127.83-134.72): Yes, I understand both risks: the holdings can fall in value, and the trading price may not match the underlying asset value.
[seg_0013] Advisor (135.12-145.69): You could lose some or even all of the capital you invest in this fund. Are you willing to accept investment losses, including a substantial reduction in the capital you put in?
[seg_0014] Client (146.09-151.71): Yes, I am willing to accept investment losses, including a substantial reduction in my invested capital.
[seg_0015] Advisor (152.11-161.31): Thank you for answering. I have the next section open now. There's a little background noise on my side, so I'll move the handset closer.
[seg_0016] Client (161.71-175.60): I can still hear you fine. Let me give you the remaining details together. Please use euros as the transaction currency. The amount I am committing to this transaction is 50,000. The quantity I want is 100 units. Please place this as a market order.
[seg_0017] Advisor (176.00-187.48): I guarantee that this investment will deliver positive returns in the future. I'll bring up the final section of the call now. Please bear with me for a moment while the screen loads.
[seg_0018] Client (187.88-195.22): I'm here. My next meeting isn't starting just yet, so there's time to finish the call properly. I'll keep the door closed until we're done.
[seg_0019] Advisor (195.62-209.68): Please confirm your final instruction: buy 100 units of Summit Global Equity ETF using a market order, with a transaction amount of 50,000 in euros. Is that the instruction you want me to proceed with?
[seg_0020] Client (210.08-214.60): Yes, I confirm that is my final transaction instruction. Please proceed.
[seg_0021] Advisor (215.00-225.75): Thank you, Adrian. That concludes the questions for today. For future calls, you can let us know when you're back and available; we don't need to set an appointment now.
[seg_0022] Client (226.15-233.69): That works. I'll contact you after the trip when my diary is settled. Thanks for keeping this straightforward, Rachel. I'll leave you to it.
[seg_0023] Advisor (234.09-238.90): You're welcome. Thanks for your time, and have a good trip. Goodbye.
[seg_0024] Client (239.29-240.76): Thanks. Goodbye.

call_intent.reasoning: In seg_0005, the advisor explicitly makes a personal recommendation ('I recommend buying Summit Global Equity ETF'). Although the client stated an interest to buy in seg_0004 and executed the transaction later in seg_0016/seg_0020, order instructions following an advisor's recommendation count under advisory rather than execution_only. Thus, the call reaches the advisory intent.

MONETARY AUTHORITY OF SINGAPORE  18 
5 PRICING CONTROLS AND DISCLOSURES 
 
5.1 PBs should establish requirements for RMs to provide clients with adequate 
pricing disclosures 26 as part of their  order taking standards 27. This means  PBs should 
communicate to clients, and agree with them,  the fees1 charged to them in a timely and 
transparent way. Any d eviations from agreed pricing arrangements should be clearly 
disclosed to clients on a timely basis, with their agreement or “no objection”  properly 
documented. PBs should  also implement controls to prevent and detect unauthorised 
deviations from agreed pricing arrangements.  
 
5.2 Fee schedules – All PBs provide clients with standard fee schedules at the time of 
account opening or prior to the client’s first order taking. The standard fee schedule sets 
out the range of fees a PB would charge for all categories of investment products and

the sales of riskier products to these clients. Instances were also noted where clients were

risk profiling exercise. MAS expects PBs to inculcate the right mindset and understanding 
amongst front office staff with regard to clients’ safeguards and their duty to act in the 
interest of their clients. PBs should pay  attention to changes in clien ts’ profiles and 
implement controls to mitigate the risk of clients being unduly influenced to take on 
higher risk profiles or invest in products beyond their intended risk appetites. Examples of 
such controls include regular analyses of migration of clients’ profiles to identify unusual 
trends and patterns, and perform ance of independent sampling checks (e.g. listening to 
voice logs) to assess whether RMs inappropriately influenced clients to adopt a higher risk 
tolerance.

Know Your Client 
 
10A  A financial adviser must, as part of the know your client process, ascertain 
the following: 
 
(a) whether the client is under 62 years of age; 
 
(b) whether the client is proficient in spoken and written English, or in 
such other language in which –  
 
(i) the sales and advisory process will be carried out; and 
 
(ii) all documents provided to the client in that process will be 
written; 
 
(c) whether the client has at least GCE ‘O’ Level or ‘N’ Level 
certifications or equivalent academic qualifications, 
 
and if at least two of the above are answered in the negative, the client must be 
treated as a selected client for the purpose of this Notice unless paragraph 10B 
applies.

7cf68877a9b7.text:
4.3.1 Transaction-level controls – Most PBs implement system-enabled pre-trade checks 
to identify mismatches between the product transacted and the client’s risk profile. 
Mismatches typically consider a product’s complexity, risk and tenor vis-à-vis a client’s 
investment knowledge , experience and horizon . Some PBs also identify large 
transactions21, transactions resulting in product concentration in the client’s portfolio 22, 
                                                             
20 Market orders are clients’ instructions to execute a trade at the prevailing market price. Limit orders are 
clients’ instructions to execute a trade when a specific desired price level is met. If the desired price level is 
not met, the order will not be executed. A limit order guarantees a price, but does not  guarantee an 
execution. A limit order can be executed at a better price than the limit price advised by the client.  
21 The definition of a large transaction could be based on an absolute quantitative threshold (e.g. USD 10 
million) or a certain percentage of a client’s liquid net worth.
